{{Short description|Australian mathematician}}
'''Edith Rita Lowenstern''' (26 December 1904 – 1970) was an Australian mathematician.

She was born in [[Dandenong]] and educated at [[Melbourne Girls Grammar School]] and the [[University of Melbourne]], where she captained the [[Melbourne University Hockey Club|women's hockey team]] in 1924–1925.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ainsworth |first1=Barbara |title=Edith Rita Lowenstern (1904–1970) |url=https://peopleaustralia.anu.edu.au/biography/lowenstern-edith-rita-31846 |website=People Australia |publisher=[[National Centre of Biography]] |access-date=13 March 2026}}</ref> She then worked as a tutor at Melbourne before being appointed as lecturer at the [[University of Tasmania]], becoming the first full-time female lecturer at that institution, as well as the second female mathematics lecturer in Australia.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Praeger |first1=Cheryl E. |author1-link=Cheryl Praeger |last2=Ward|first2=Lesley A.|author2-link=Lesley Ward|title=Women Working in Mathematics in Australian Universities, and the Women in Mathematics Special Interest Group (WIMSIG) |url=https://api.research-repository.uwa.edu.au/ws/portalfiles/portal/491552822/WIMSIG_2.pdf |publisher=Women in Mathematics Special Interest Group |access-date=13 March 2026}}</ref>

Lowenstern resigned in 1936, married, and moved to [[Bicheno]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The Mysterious Miss Lowenstern |url=https://125timeline.utas.edu.au/timeline/1930/mysterious-miss-lowenstern/ |publisher=[[University of Tasmania]] |access-date=13 March 2026}}</ref>
